svg.title: The representational ceiling
svg.desc: Log-log chart plotting usable corpus size against embedding dimension. Weller et al. empirical fit (coral line) passes through two labeled anchor points: d=768 with n≈1.7M documents (open-weights default) and d=4096 with n≈250M (current frontier). Shaded unreachable region above the line. Formula at top: d ≥ log C(n,k) / log(1+1/γ). Benchmark strip reports LIMIT (50K docs, 1K queries) with E5-Mistral, GritLM, Qwen3 below 20% Recall@100 at d=4096 while BM25 reaches 93.6% Recall@100; GTE-ModernColBERT (vector-per-token) recovers 54.8% Recall@100 on the same set.
svg.text: FIG 01 / WHERE THE GEOMETRY RUNS OUT
For single-vector retrievers, the embedding dimension d
sets a hard ceiling on the number of distinct top-k rankings
the space can represent. Below that ceiling, some rankings
Some top-k sets cannot be represented
at this dimension. No reranker or
GTE-ModernColBERT keeps one vector per token
The ceiling is single-vector geometry, not retrieval.
Scaling the retrieve-read-generate loop scales the bill
without moving the curve. Raise d, change retriever grammar,
